name: obs-mcp-native
description: Rust OBS MCP service with immutable production and advanced profiles
long_description: Host-specific Rust service for darwin/arm64. Node.js and the JavaScript MCP SDK are not installed or run by this extension. Choose an existing approved private state directory before startup. Discovery works while OBS is offline. The 178-name catalog is a union of immutable profiles, not simultaneous tool availability: Production exposes up to 164 with approved host/media adapters; Advanced exposes 163 and excludes guarded Take/media/Stage/recovery owners. Read-only and dynamic tool groups narrow discovery further. Native transport/platform qualification is separate from package contents; consult docs/native-distribution.md for current prerequisites and limits.

obs_websocket_url.title: OBS WebSocket URL
obs_websocket_url.description: WebSocket URL for OBS Studio. Configure in OBS: Tools → WebSocket Server Settings

obs_websocket_password.title: OBS WebSocket Password
obs_websocket_password.description: Password from OBS WebSocket Server Settings. Leave empty if authentication is disabled.

obs_mcp_toolsets.title: Tool groups
obs_mcp_toolsets.description: Comma-separated tool groups to expose: all, core, or any of general, scenes, scene-items, sources, inputs, media, filters, transitions, record, stream, outputs, config, ui, protocol.

obs_mcp_read_only.title: Read-only mode
obs_mcp_read_only.description: Expose only tools that do not change OBS.

obs_mcp_confirm_live.title: Confirm live actions
obs_mcp_confirm_live.description: Ask before starting, stopping, or toggling a stream or generic output, and before stopping or toggling recording.

obs_mcp_dynamic_toolsets.title: Load tool groups on demand
obs_mcp_dynamic_toolsets.description: Start with only the tool groups above (or just general) and let the model turn others on as it needs them.

obs_mcp_read_obs_config.title: Use the password saved in OBS
obs_mcp_read_obs_config.description: When no password is entered above, read the one OBS saved on this computer.

obs_mcp_state_dir.title: Approved private state directory
obs_mcp_state_dir.description: Required existing absolute directory owned by you, with safe private permissions (0700 on Unix). Stores endpoint-bound operation journals and snapshots. Create and approve it explicitly; the extension does not initialize a new home directory or erase history.

obs_mcp_native_profile.title: Native capability profile
obs_mcp_native_profile.description: production (default) or advanced. Advanced permits manual/raw/vendor/hotkey effects but never creates guarded Take/media/Stage/recovery owners. Possible advanced effects durably block later guarded reentry in the same endpoint/state namespace; restarting MCP does not clear this.

obs_mcp_recording_root.title: Approved recording directory (optional)
obs_mcp_recording_root.description: Existing approved private recording directory for Production Take/Clip/file workflows. Leave empty for inspection and other available workflows. Advanced ignores guarded-owner configuration. Availability depends on validated local adapters and media tools.

obs_mcp_ffmpeg.title: FFmpeg executable (optional)
obs_mcp_ffmpeg.description: Existing trusted FFmpeg executable used for local media inspection/processing. If omitted, discovery uses PATH. No executable is downloaded or installed by this extension.

obs_mcp_ffprobe.title: ffprobe executable (optional)
obs_mcp_ffprobe.description: Existing trusted ffprobe executable used for local media inspection/processing. If omitted, discovery uses PATH. No executable is downloaded or installed by this extension.

tools.name: obs-batch
tools.description: Send several requests from the pinned OBS WebSocket protocol in one message. serial-realtime runs them in order as fast as possible; serial-frame runs one per rendered frame, so changes such as hiding one source and showing another land on the same frame. Sleep ({sleepMillis} or {sleepFrames}) pauses serial batches. Each request succeeds or fails on its own unless haltOnFailure is set

tools.name: obs-preflight
tools.description: Check for the conditions that make OBS silently refuse or botch a recording: an active recording, an invalid output path, low disk space, an unusable encoder, unapplied output settings, audible inputs, and blank (0×0) sources. Read-only; run it before obs-start-record

tools.name: obs-record-clip
tools.description: Record a clip of up to 50s in one call: runs obs-preflight, starts recording and waits for OBS to confirm, adds chapter markers, stops, then checks the file's length and audio with ffprobe/ffmpeg when available. For longer takes use obs-start-record and obs-stop-record

tools.name: obs-capture-window
tools.description: Resolve a macOS ScreenCaptureKit or Linux X11 window using an existing compatible capture as read-only inventory, then create/reuse the capture, fit it and optionally silence it. Refuses missing or ambiguous discovery before changes. apply:false returns a plan without snapshots, mutations or screenshots. Mac application auto-discovery is refused; configure and bind an existing application capture in OBS. Linux application matching selects one window. Wayland portal selection requires the user: configure a PipeWire window capture in OBS, then use backend:portal without window/application to fit and inspect it. Returns capture size and optional screenshot; inspect the picture for target correctness.

tools.name: obs-take-start
tools.description: Start a watched recording of any length: runs obs-preflight, starts recording and waits for OBS to confirm, then watches audio, frames, and picture until obs-take-stop. Mark steps with obs-take-mark and check progress with obs-take-status. By default, profile, scene collection, and output setting changes are refused until the take stops

tools.name: obs-take-mark
tools.description: Add a named chapter to the running take, in the file (Hybrid MP4/MOV) and in the take log

tools.name: obs-take-status
tools.description: Report the running take: length, file size, loudest recorded input, skipped frames, black or unchanging picture, chapters, and warnings so far

tools.name: obs-take-stop
tools.description: Stop the running take: stops recording, then checks the file's length and audio with ffprobe/ffmpeg when available, reports what the monitor saw, and writes <name>.take.json next to a local recording

tools.name: obs-prepare-demo
tools.description: Plan by default. Fit and silence one existing macOS, Linux X11 or authorized PipeWire window capture in the exact current collection/program scene. Refuses live output, shared sources, groups, missing identity/state, and unpersisted recovery. Does not retarget or create anything. No UI exclusion guarantee.

tools.name: obs-recover-demo
tools.description: Plan by default. Restore only fields owned by the given durable preparation journal. Refuses conflicting operator changes, different identities/collection, and active output. Rereads postconditions; partial failure needs inspection before retry. Legacy snapshots require manual obs-restore.

tools.name: obs-trim-take
tools.description: Plan, and optionally export, a copy of a recording with its dead time cut: stretches where the picture does not change (and the sound, if any, is silent). A spinner or shimmering label counts as unchanged; text appearing does not. Keeps a little of each stretch, holds each step's result before the next chapter and the end, and moves chapters to match. Without apply it only returns the plan. Export requires 8-bit SDR input and a qualified H.264 encoder; validates metadata and full decode before publishing a new copy. Needs ffmpeg; works on files in the OBS recording directory

tools.name: obs-contact-sheet
tools.description: Return one image of frames from a recording, tiled in time order: at each chapter start by default, or at the given times. Use it to check a take or an edit without watching it. Needs ffmpeg; works on files in the OBS recording directory

tools.name: obs-snapshot
tools.description: Save the current settings, mute, volume, and audio tracks of inputs, and the transform, visibility, lock, and order of scene items, so obs-restore can undo later changes. Defaults to the program scene and the inputs in it. Snapshots are saved on disk (the last 20) and survive restarts; call with list: true to see them

tools.name: obs-restore
tools.description: Return inputs and scene items to a snapshot from obs-snapshot, changing only what differs, in one request batch. dryRun lists the changes without making them. Removed items and inputs cannot be recreated, and items added since are left in place; both are reported

tools.name: obs-apply-scene
tools.description: Describe a scene and let the server make OBS match it: creates the scene, inputs, and items that are missing, and sets only the settings, visibility, lock, audio, transforms, and order that differ. Without apply it returns the plan. Applies in two request batches, checks the result, warns about sources that render at 0×0, and saves a snapshot first so obs-restore can undo changes to existing sources

tools.name: obs-audit-scene
tools.description: Read a specifically selected scene and report structural pass, fail, or unknown checks with item occurrence identities. Optional screenshot supports separate visual review. A structural pass does not establish correct rendered content or recording readiness. Does not alter OBS.

tools.name: obs-plan-scene-template
tools.description: Resolve portable logical roles against exact local collection/canvas/source/occurrence bindings. Flat layouts and literal transforms only. Returns proposed changes and explicit blockers for missing/duplicate bindings, renamed/replaced sources, incompatible kinds, nested scenes, and wrong canvas. Never sends mutation requests.

tools.name: obs-stage-scene
tools.description: Stage an exact existing scene in Studio Mode preview, include its screenshot, and issue a short-lived one-use stageId. Rechecks dependencies and program before/after staging. Does not edit inputs, filters, audio, or layout; shared inputs remain shared. Inspect the image before obs-take-scene.

tools.name: obs-take-scene
tools.description: Consume a stageId once. Recheck the staged subject, program, preview, connection and Studio Mode; dispatch one transition; separately report request acceptance and whether the intended scene is observed on program. Never blindly retry uncertain outcomes. Rendered content still requires inspection.
